english.title: Combine with seamen to disobey command / neglect duty or impede progress/navigation on ship
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a seaman employed in a United Kingdom ship, namely **(..SPECIFY SHIP..), combined with other seamen employed in that ship to

(A)_[disobey lawful commands, namely **(..SPECIFY COMMANDS..), which were required to be obeyed at a time while the ship was]_
(B)_[neglect a duty, namely **(..SPECIFY DUTY..), which was required to be discharged at a time while the ship was]_
(C)_[impede the progress of the ship's voyage at a time while it was]_
(D)_[impede the navigation of the ship at a time while it was]_

at sea
english.legislation: Contrary to section 59 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
seaman employed in a UK ship
combined with other seamen employed in that ship
to disobey lawful commands required
to be obeyed whilst ship was at sea /
neglected a duty which was required
to be discharged whilst ship was at sea /
impeded at a time when the ship was at sea
the progress of a voyage / navigation of the ship

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 59(2) of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995 states that for the purposes of this section a ship shall be treated as being at sea at any time when it is not securely moored in a safe berth.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
